sentences.text: In these writ petitions, the common issue raised by the petitioners is relating to lapse of acquisition proceedings on account of failure on the part of respondent authorities to award compensation despite lands in question are being acquired and utilised for the NC: 2023:KHC-K:7287 C/W WP No.202262/2019, purpose of construction of bridge-cum-barrage at Bhima river.

2. Relevant facts for adjudication of the case are that the petitioners in all these writ petitions claim to be the owners in possession of the various lands as stated in the writ petitions and respondents have acquired the portion of the land belonging to the petitioners for the purpose of construction of bridge-cum-barrage of Bhima River by invoking urgency clause under Section 4(1) read with Section 17 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') as per notification dated 23.08.2005.

Thereafter, respondent authorities have issued notification under Section 6(1)
read with Section 17 of the Act as per Annexure-D.
Pursuant to the same, the fourth respondent - SLAO passed consent award on 10.10.2008 and 18.09.2008 under Section 11 (2) of the Act.

It is the grievance of the petitioners that though the land belonging to the petitioners have been acquired,
however, compensation NC: 2023:KHC-K:7287 C/W WP No.202262/2019, has not been deposited before the Court or before the appropriate authority by the respondents herein.

Therefore, the petitioners have raised plea that the acquisition proceedings have lapsed on account of Section 24(2)
of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation,
Resettlement Act 2013 (for short, hereinafter referred to as 'Act of 2013').

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation,
Resettlement Act 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Hence, these writ petitions are filed.

3. I have heard Sri.A.M.Biradar, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and Smt. Archana P.Tiwari, learned Additional Advocate General appearing on behalf of Sri.Gopalkrishna B. Yadav,
learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent Nos.1, 2 and 4 and Sri.Krupa Sagar Patil,
learned counsel appearing for respondent No.3.
Sham Rao And Ors vs The Secretary And Ors on 12 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26970596/
6

4. Sri A.M.Biradar, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners while inviting the attention of the Court to provision under Section 24(2) of the Act submitted that NC: 2023:KHC-K:7287 C/W WP No.202262/2019, since the property belonging to the petitioners have been acquired and utilised for construction of bridge-cum- barrage of Bhima river, however, compensation has been denied and accordingly, sought for interference of this Court.

5. Per contra, Sri.Krupa Sagar Patil, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.3-beneficiary of the land submitted that pursuant to the passing of the award under the Act, compensation has been deposited with the fourth respondent and therefore, negatives the submission made by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners.

6. Smt. Archana P.Tiwari, learned Additional Advocate General argued that it is not the case of lapse insofar as acquisition proceedings are concerned, however, she fairly admits that the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the Act of 2013.

It is submitted by the learned Additional Advocate General that the - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7287 C/W WP No.202262/2019, compensation was not awarded to the petitioners in view of enquiry being pending consideration with the Department of Irrigation and accordingly, sought for disposal of the writ petition.

7. Having taken note of the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties, it is not in dispute that the lands belonging to the petitioners have been acquired by the respondent authorities by exercising provision under section 4(1) read with section 17 of the Act.
Final notification was issued under the Act and award came to be passed on 10.10.2008 and 18.09.2008 under Section 11 (2) of the Act.
However, respondent No.4 has addressed letters to the petitioners as per Annexure-F series during 2018 fixing the compensation to be awarded to the petitioners herein.

8. Taking into consideration the declaration of law made by the Constitutional Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Indore Development Authority vs.
- 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7287 C/W WP No.202262/2019, Manohar Lal and Others reported in 2020 (8)
SCC 129, I am of the view that as the award has been passed much before the commencement of Act of 2013 and compensation has not reached the petitioners and therefore, the contention of the petitioners that the acquisition proceedings are lapsed cannot be considered, however, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the provisions of Act of 2013.

sentences.text: It is also not disputed that the entire project is concluded.
9. In that view of the matter, the writ petitions are disposed of.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
7. Having taken note of the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties, it is not in dispute that the lands belonging to the petitioners have been acquired by the respondent authorities by exercising provision under section 4(1) read with section 17 of the Act.
8. Taking into consideration the declaration of law made by the Constitutional Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Indore Development Authority vs.
- 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7287 C/W WP No.202262/2019, Manohar Lal and Others reported in 2020 (8)
SCC 129, I am of the view that as the award has been passed much before the commencement of Act of 2013 and compensation has not reached the petitioners and therefore, the contention of the petitioners that the acquisition proceedings are lapsed cannot be considered, however, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the provisions of Act of 2013.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Final notification was issued under the Act and award came to be passed on 10.10.2008 and 18.09.2008 under Section 11 (2) of the Act.
9. In that view of the matter, the writ petitions are disposed of.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation under the provisions of Act of 2013.
Needless to say that the respondent No.4 herein shall redetermine the compensation in terms of the Act of 2013 taking into account the date on which the possession has been taken as well as recourse to issuing of notification dated - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:7287 C/W WP No.202262/2019, 23.08.2005 under section 4 (1) read with section 17 of the Act.
11. It is also made clear that the petitioners are also entitled for all consequential benefits.
